note.explanation: Choose the network type by looking at the size and area it covers. A few personal devices nearby use a PAN; devices in one home, school, or office use a LAN; multiple LANs across a campus use a CAN or across a city use a MAN; a very large geographical area uses a WAN.
examples: A smartphone connected to a wireless headset by Bluetooth forms a PAN.
A network connecting different branch offices of a company across countries is a WAN.
note.simple: Think about how far the network reaches: personal devices, one local place, a campus, a city, or a very large area.
note.checkQuestion: What type of network connects several LANs within a university campus?
note.title: Choosing a network type by its coverage
steps: Identify the area covered by the network.
Check whether it connects personal devices, one limited area, a campus, a city, or a large geographical area.
Match that area to PAN, LAN, CAN, MAN, or WAN.
note.answer: A CAN connects multiple LANs within a limited geographical area, such as a university campus.

mcqs.stem: A smartphone communicates with a wireless headset over a few meters. Which type of network is this?
rationales: This is correct because a PAN connects personal devices over a short range.
This is incorrect because a LAN connects devices within a limited area such as a home or school.
This is incorrect because a MAN spans a city or large campus and connects multiple LANs.
This is incorrect because a WAN covers a large geographical area and connects LANs and MANs.

options: A personal-device connection over a few meters
mcqs.stem: Which situation is the best example of a LAN?
rationales: This is correct because a LAN connects devices within a limited area such as a school.
This is incorrect because a network spanning a city is a MAN.
This is incorrect because a network across countries is a WAN.
This is incorrect because a short-range connection between personal devices is a PAN.

mcqs.stem: Several LANs in different buildings of one university are connected within the campus. Which network type best fits?
rationales: This is incorrect because a PAN connects personal devices over a short range.
This is incorrect because a LAN covers a limited area, rather than multiple campus LANs.
This is correct because a CAN connects multiple LANs within a limited geographical area such as a university campus.
This is incorrect because a WAN covers a large geographical area.

mcqs.stem: A network connects several LANs in different parts of one city. Which type is it?
rationales: This is incorrect because a PAN connects personal devices within a short range.
This is incorrect because a LAN is limited to an area such as a home, school, or office building.
This is correct because a MAN spans a city and connects multiple LANs.
This is incorrect because a CAN connects LANs within a limited area such as a campus.

mcqs.stem: Which network type covers a large geographical area and can connect multiple LANs and MANs?
rationales: This is incorrect because a PAN is a small, short-range network for personal devices.
This is incorrect because a LAN covers a limited area.
This is incorrect because a MAN spans a city or a large campus.
This is correct because a WAN covers a large geographical area and connects multiple LANs and MANs.

mcqs.stem: Which is given as the largest example of a WAN?
rationales: This is correct because the section identifies the Internet as the largest example of a WAN.
This is incorrect because a computer lab is an example of a LAN.
This is incorrect because a short-range personal-device connection is a PAN.
This is incorrect because a network within a university campus is a CAN.

mcqs.stem: What is the typical range of a PAN, according to the section?
rationales: This is correct because the section says a PAN typically covers a few meters.
This is incorrect because a country-wide range is not the typical range of a PAN.
This is incorrect because the section gives a few meters, not a fixed single-room limit.
This is incorrect because a PAN is a short-range personal network, not a worldwide network.

examTips: A board question may ask you to define or identify PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, or CAN from its coverage area.
For a definition question, include both the coverage area and what the network connects.
For an example question, connect the example to its range: a school lab is a LAN, a university campus can be a CAN, a city-wide connection is a MAN, and a network across countries is a WAN.

example.question: The computer network in your school that connects all the computers in the lab is a LAN. What type of network is it?

explain.title: Personal Area Network (PAN)
explain.body: A PAN is a small network used for communication between personal devices, such as smartphones, tablets, and laptops, within a short range. For example, Bluetooth connections between a smartphone and a wireless headset form a PAN. Its range is typically a few meters.

explain.title: Local Area Network (LAN)
explain.body: A LAN is a network that connects computers and devices within a limited area, such as a home, school, or office building. A school computer network connecting all the computers in a lab is an example.

explain.title: Metropolitan Area Network (MAN)
explain.body: A MAN is a network that spans a city or a large campus, connecting multiple LANs together. It can cover an area of up to 50 kilometers.

explain.title: Wide Area Network (WAN)
explain.body: A WAN covers a large geographical area, connecting multiple LANs and MANs. The Internet is the largest example of a WAN.

explain.title: Campus Area Network (CAN)
explain.body: A CAN is a network that connects multiple LANs within a limited geographical area, such as a university campus or a business park.

mistakes: Do not mix up a MAN and a WAN: a MAN spans a city or large campus, while a WAN covers a large geographical area.
Do not call every network in a university a MAN. A network connecting LANs within the campus is a CAN.
Do not describe a LAN as covering a whole city; a LAN is limited to places such as a home, school, or office building.
Remember that a PAN is for personal devices over a short range, typically a few meters.
